title: Allow playing a stream on multiple arbitrary outputs
line: The Audio settings page has a new Combine Outputs button that creates a playback device which plays on several chosen devices at once.
explanation: Plasma had no way to send sound to more than one output device at the same time: the Audio page and the volume widget only let you pick one device, and the old 'simultaneous output on all local sound cards' option is PulseAudio-only and hidden on PipeWire. The Pulse API can't attach one stream to several devices, but both PulseAudio and PipeWire provide module-combine-sink, which makes a virtual device that forwards to chosen devices. The Audio page now has 'Combine Outputs…', a dialog to tick two or more playback devices; it creates a device named after them (e.g. 'Speakers + Headphones') that can be the default or picked per app, with a Remove button. The list is saved in plasmaparc and kded recreates it at login and re-adds devices that come back later, like Bluetooth headphones; the volume widget shows it even with 'Show virtual devices' off.

commits.message:
kcm: add a way to combine outputs into one playback device

There was no way in Plasma to play a stream on several chosen outputs at
once. Add "Combine Outputs…" to the Audio page, which creates a playback
device that plays on the checked devices, kept across logins by kded.

BUG: 440536
